title: Week 1: Quantum Foundations
description: Fundamental quantum mechanics: Planck hypothesis, photoelectric effect, de Broglie wavelength, uncertainty principle, and wave equations.

questions.question: Which branch of physics primarily deals with the behavior of matter and energy at atomic and subatomic scales?
questions.explanation: Quantum mechanics explains the behavior of matter and energy at atomic and subatomic scales.

questions.question: According to Planck’s hypothesis, electromagnetic energy is emitted in the form of
questions.explanation: Planck proposed that energy is emitted or absorbed in discrete packets called quanta.

questions.question: Which phenomenon demonstrates the particle nature of light?
questions.explanation: The photoelectric effect demonstrates the particle nature of light because electrons are emitted only when photons carry sufficient energy.

questions.question: According to de Broglie hypothesis, the wavelength associated with a particle is given by
questions.explanation: According to de Broglie hypothesis, λ = h/p, where h is Planck’s constant and p is momentum.

questions.question: Which principle states that position and momentum of a particle cannot be simultaneously known with perfect accuracy?
questions.explanation: The Heisenberg uncertainty principle states that position and momentum cannot both be measured exactly at the same time.

questions.question: Quantum tunneling occurs because particles possess
questions.explanation: Quantum tunneling occurs because particles exhibit wave-like behavior and have non-zero probability of crossing potential barriers.

questions.question: The Schrödinger equation in quantum mechanics is fundamentally a
questions.explanation: The Schrödinger equation is a linear differential equation describing quantum wave functions.

questions.question: The square magnitude of the wave function |Ψ(x,t)|^2 represents
questions.explanation: The probability density is given by P(x,t) = |Ψ(x,t)|^2.

questions.question: For a physically acceptable wave function, the wave function must be
questions.explanation: A physically acceptable wave function must be finite, continuous, and single-valued.

questions.question: For a free particle with definite momentum, the probability density is
questions.explanation: For a free particle with definite momentum, the probability density remains constant everywhere.

title: Week 2: Cryogenic CMOS & Body Effect
description: CMOS operation at low temperatures, carrier mobility enhancement, threshold voltage shifts, body effect, DIBL, and velocity saturation.

questions.question: What is the primary advantage of operating CMOS devices at cryogenic temperatures?
questions.explanation: Cryogenic operation significantly reduces thermal noise, improving signal integrity in quantum computing electronics.

questions.question: At cryogenic temperatures, the carrier mobility in MOSFETs generally
questions.explanation: Reduced phonon scattering at low temperatures increases carrier mobility.

questions.question: What happens to the threshold voltage of a MOSFET at cryogenic temperatures?
questions.explanation: At cryogenic temperatures, incomplete ionization and other effects generally increase MOSFET threshold voltage.

questions.question: Which effect causes threshold voltage to increase when substrate bias becomes more negative in an NMOS transistor?
questions.explanation: When substrate bias changes, threshold voltage changes due to body effect.

questions.question: Drain-Induced Barrier Lowering (DIBL) causes the threshold voltage to
questions.explanation: DIBL reduces threshold voltage as drain voltage increases.

questions.question: What happens to the effective channel length in channel-length modulation?
options: It becomes equal to oxide thickness
questions.explanation: In channel-length modulation, effective channel length decreases with increasing drain voltage.

questions.question: The body effect coefficient in a MOSFET is generally denoted by
questions.explanation: The body effect coefficient is represented by γ.

questions.question: Why is body effect generally considered undesirable in MOS circuits?
questions.explanation: Body effect changes threshold voltage with substrate bias and increases threshold voltage variation.

questions.question: In a MOS capacitor C-V characteristic, the capacitance becomes minimum in the
questions.explanation: In the inversion region, the depletion width becomes maximum for high frequency, minimizing capacitance.

questions.question: Velocity saturation in MOSFETs occurs because carrier velocity
options: Becomes independent of electric field at high fields
questions.explanation: At high electric fields, carrier velocity saturates and no longer increases proportionally with field.

title: Week 3: Freeze-Out & Scattering
description: Cryostat thermal radiation shields, incomplete ionization (freeze-out), Fermi level shifts, Boltzmann approximation, and phonon suppression.

questions.question: What is the primary function of radiation shielding in a cryostat?
questions.explanation: Radiation shields reduce heat transfer due to thermal radiation and improve cryostat efficiency.

questions.question: As temperature decreases, incomplete ionization in semiconductors causes
questions.explanation: At very low temperatures, dopants may not ionize completely, causing carrier freeze-out.

questions.question: In an n-type semiconductor, increasing donor concentration shifts the Fermi level
questions.explanation: Increasing donor concentration moves the Fermi level closer to the conduction band.

questions.question: Which approximation is commonly used for carrier concentration calculations under non-degenerate conditions?
questions.explanation: Under non-degenerate conditions, carrier statistics are simplified using the Boltzmann approximation.

questions.question: Which scattering mechanism becomes less dominant at cryogenic temperatures?
questions.explanation: Phonon scattering decreases strongly at cryogenic temperatures because lattice vibrations reduce.

questions.question: What happens to carrier mobility at low temperatures when phonon scattering reduces?
questions.explanation: Reduced phonon scattering improves carrier mobility at low temperatures.

questions.question: The intrinsic carrier concentration of silicon at cryogenic temperature becomes
questions.explanation: Intrinsic carrier concentration decreases drastically at cryogenic temperatures because thermal generation becomes negligible.

questions.question: Which quantity mainly determines the probability of occupation of electron energy states?
questions.explanation: The Fermi level determines occupation probability of electronic energy states.

questions.question: In compensated semiconductors, the effective donor concentration is approximately given by
questions.explanation: For compensated semiconductors, effective donor concentration becomes Neff = ND − NA.

questions.question: Why is cryogenic operation advantageous for quantum computing electronics?
options: It reduces thermal noise and improves coherence
questions.explanation: Cryogenic operation reduces thermal noise and improves quantum coherence, which is essential for quantum computing systems.

title: Week 4: Varshni Model & Bandgap
description: Temperature-dependent bandgap widening (Varshni equation), impurity scattering dominance, depletion charge scaling, and corrected Fermi potential.

questions.question: At cryogenic temperatures, which scattering mechanism becomes dominant in semiconductor devices?
questions.explanation: At low temperatures, lattice vibrations reduce significantly, making impurity scattering dominant.

questions.question: According to the Varshni model, what happens to the semiconductor bandgap as temperature decreases?
questions.explanation: According to the Varshni model, semiconductor bandgap widens as temperature decreases.

questions.question: The depletion charge density in a MOS structure is proportional to
questions.explanation: The depletion charge depends on substrate doping as Qd proportional to √NA.

questions.question: If the probability of occupation of an energy state equals 0.5, then the energy level is equal to
questions.explanation: For the Fermi-Dirac distribution, occupation probability becomes 0.5 when energy equals the Fermi level.

questions.question: What happens to the resistance of heavily doped silicon at cryogenic temperatures?
questions.explanation: In heavily doped silicon, higher carrier concentration reduces resistance despite mobility degradation.

questions.question: Which factor mainly contributes to increased threshold voltage at cryogenic temperatures?
questions.explanation: Bandgap widening at cryogenic temperatures increases threshold voltage.

questions.question: What is the major competing effect against bandgap widening at low temperatures?
questions.explanation: Incomplete dopant ionization (freeze-out) competes against bandgap widening effects.

questions.question: At cryogenic temperatures, the Fermi level in p-type silicon tends to move
questions.explanation: At cryogenic temperatures in p-type silicon, the Fermi level shifts closer to the valence band.

questions.question: Why does intrinsic carrier concentration decrease significantly at low temperatures?
questions.explanation: As bandgap increases at low temperatures, thermal generation decreases and intrinsic carrier concentration reduces drastically.

questions.question: In the presence of freeze-out, the corrected bulk Fermi potential is approximately expressed as
questions.explanation: Corrected bulk Fermi potential under freeze-out is ΦF* = ΦF − ΔΦF.

title: Week 5: Poole-Frenkel & Subthreshold
description: Field-assisted ionization via Poole-Frenkel effect, subthreshold slope steepening, ON-current boost, thermal noise reduction, and carrier dwell time.

questions.question: The Poole–Frenkel effect is significant in cryogenic devices because
options: It enables ionization of dopants via electric fields
It increases the thermal generation rate
It reduces the threshold voltage directly
questions.explanation: At low temperatures, field-assisted ionization through the Poole–Frenkel effect becomes crucial for activating frozen-out dopants.

questions.question: At cryogenic temperatures, till 100K, the subthreshold slope of a MOSFET generally
questions.explanation: Since subthreshold swing is proportional to temperature, it improves (decreases) at low temperatures.

questions.question: Which parameter primarily determines the subthreshold swing of a MOSFET?
questions.explanation: Subthreshold swing depends strongly on temperature (S proportional to T).

questions.question: At cryogenic temperatures, the ON-current of a MOSFET generally increases because of
questions.explanation: At low temperatures, improved carrier mobility increases ON-current.

questions.question: Which effect causes the threshold voltage to increase at cryogenic temperatures?
questions.explanation: Bandgap widening at low temperature contributes to an increase in threshold voltage.

questions.question: In a MOSFET operating in the subthreshold region, the drain current depends on gate voltage
questions.explanation: In the subthreshold region, ID is proportional to exp(VGS / nVT), showing exponential dependence.

questions.question: Which parameter is most directly affected by dopant freeze-out?
questions.explanation: Freeze-out reduces the number of ionized dopants and therefore reduces carrier concentration.

questions.question: Why are cryogenic MOSFET models different from room-temperature models?
questions.explanation: Cryogenic operation changes mobility, threshold voltage, carrier statistics, and freeze-out behavior, requiring specialized models.

questions.question: At low temperatures, which noise component is reduced significantly?
questions.explanation: Thermal noise power decreases directly with temperature.

questions.question: What is dwell time in semiconductor physics?
options: Carrier transport time across the channel
Time taken to generate carriers thermally
Average time a carrier remains trapped
questions.explanation: Dwell time refers to how long a carrier stays trapped in a localized state before being released.

title: Week 6: Scattering & Ballistic Transport
description: Ionized impurity vs surface roughness scattering, Matthiessen's rule, backscattering model, critical length l0, ballistic transport, and FinFETs.

questions.question: At cryogenic temperatures, which scattering mechanism predominantly limits mobility at low inversion charge density?
questions.explanation: At low temperatures and low inversion charge density, ionized impurity scattering dominates because phonon scattering is greatly reduced.

questions.question: As temperature decreases, phonon scattering in silicon MOSFETs generally
questions.explanation: Lattice vibrations decrease with temperature, reducing phonon scattering and improving mobility.

questions.question: The effective electric field Eeff used in mobility modeling depends primarily on
questions.explanation: The effective field model uses both inversion and depletion charge contributions to characterize mobility degradation.

questions.question: Which scattering mechanism becomes dominant at high vertical electric fields in MOSFETs?
questions.explanation: At high vertical electric fields, carriers interact strongly with the interface, making surface roughness scattering dominant.

questions.question: The Matthiessen rule is used to combine
questions.explanation: Matthiessen's rule combines multiple scattering mechanisms into an effective mobility (1/μ_eff = sum of 1/μ_i).

questions.question: In the backscattering model, a lower backscattering coefficient indicates
questions.explanation: A lower backscattering coefficient means fewer carriers are reflected backward and more travel toward the drain.

questions.question: If the reflection coefficient r = 0, the transport is
questions.explanation: For r = 0, transport is perfectly ballistic.

questions.question: The critical length l0 in a MOSFET is associated with
questions.explanation: The critical length is the source-side region where carrier backscattering significantly affects transport.

questions.question: Which transport mechanism becomes increasingly important as channel length approaches the carrier mean free path?
questions.explanation: As channel length becomes comparable to mean free path, ballistic transport becomes important.

questions.question: Why are FinFETs attractive for cryogenic electronics?
questions.explanation: FinFETs provide excellent electrostatic control and reduced short-channel effects, which remain beneficial at cryogenic temperatures.

title: Week 7: C-V Characteristics & Noise
description: MOS capacitor C-V profiling, fixed oxide charge, flat-band voltage shift, interface traps, hysteresis, and 1/f flicker noise.

questions.question: For an ideal MOS capacitor under accumulation, the measured capacitance is approximately equal to
questions.explanation: In accumulation, measured capacitance approaches the oxide capacitance.

questions.question: In a p-type MOS capacitor, a sufficiently positive gate voltage results in
questions.explanation: A positive gate voltage on a p-type substrate attracts electrons and forms inversion.

questions.question: Which charge is primarily responsible for shifting the flat-band voltage from its ideal value?
questions.explanation: Fixed oxide charge shifts the flat-band voltage from its ideal value.

questions.question: At high frequency, the inversion-layer carriers cannot respond to the AC signal because
options: Minority carrier generation is too slow
questions.explanation: At high frequency, minority carriers cannot be generated quickly enough to follow the AC signal.

questions.question: Which region of the C–V curve exhibits the minimum capacitance in a high-frequency measurement?
questions.explanation: In strong inversion (at high frequency), maximum depletion width corresponds to minimum capacitance.

questions.question: The presence of interface traps generally causes
questions.explanation: Interface traps exchange charge with the semiconductor, producing frequency dispersion.

questions.question: If a MOS capacitor has an oxide capacitance of 10 pF and a depletion capacitance of 10 pF, the measured capacitance is closest to
Hysteresis observed in a C–V curve is mainly associated with
questions.explanation: Hysteresis arises from charge trapping and de-trapping in oxide or interface traps.

questions.question: Which parameter can be extracted from the accumulation capacitance of a MOS capacitor?
questions.explanation: Oxide thickness can be extracted directly from accumulation capacitance.

questions.question: Which type of noise exhibits a power spectral density inversely proportional to frequency?
questions.explanation: Flicker noise is also known as 1/f noise.

title: Week 8: Cryo-LNAs & ADCs
description: Cryo-Low Noise Amplifiers (LNAs), ENOB, SNDR, cryogenic multiplexers, circulators, thermal cooling power limits, and PLL phase noise.

questions.question: What does ENOB stand for in ADC performance evaluation?
questions.explanation: ENOB represents the actual usable resolution after accounting for noise and distortion.

questions.question: Which parameter accounts for both noise and distortion in an ADC?
questions.explanation: SNDR combines the effects of noise and harmonic distortion.

questions.question: The primary objective of a Cryo-LNA is to achieve
questions.explanation: Cryo-LNAs are optimized primarily for very low noise figure.

questions.question: Which noise source becomes relatively more significant as the temperature decreases?
questions.explanation: Thermal noise decreases strongly at low temperatures, making flicker noise relatively more prominent.

questions.question: Cryo-LNAs are primarily used in
questions.explanation: Cryo-LNAs amplify weak quantum-readout signals with minimal added noise.

questions.question: The main purpose of cryogenic multiplexers is to
questions.explanation: Multiplexers reduce the number of wires entering the cryostat, thereby reducing heat load.

questions.question: A circulator used in quantum systems is typically a
questions.explanation: A circulator routes signals directionally between three ports as a non-reciprocal device.

questions.question: Why must power dissipation be minimized in cryogenic systems?
questions.explanation: Cryogenic refrigerators provide limited cooling power, so dissipation must be strictly minimized.

questions.question: PLL phase noise mainly affects
questions.explanation: Excess PLL phase noise introduces timing errors and reduces qubit fidelity.

questions.question: Which block is generally placed closest to the qubit readout path to minimize added noise?
questions.explanation: The first amplification stage is typically the Cryo-LNA to preserve signal integrity.

title: Week 9: Quantum Fundamentals & Entanglement
description: Qubit states, superposition, Hadamard and CNOT gates, Bell states, quantum teleportation, superdense coding, no-cloning theorem, and QKD.

questions.question: A qubit can exist in
questions.explanation: A qubit may exist in a superposition of |0⟩ and |1⟩.

questions.question: Which of the following is a cryogenic sensor?
questions.explanation: TES (Transition Edge Sensor) is a commonly used cryogenic sensor.

questions.question: What is the primary function of a Hadamard gate?
questions.explanation: The Hadamard gate converts a basis state into a superposition state.

questions.question: Entanglement refers to
options: A unique quantum correlation between qubits
questions.explanation: Entanglement is a unique quantum correlation between qubits.

questions.question: Which gate combination is commonly used to generate an entangled Bell pair?
questions.explanation: A Hadamard gate followed by a CNOT gate creates a Bell pair.

questions.question: Measurement of a qubit in superposition results in
questions.explanation: Measurement causes a superposition state to collapse to a definite basis state.

questions.question: Quantum teleportation requires
questions.explanation: Quantum teleportation requires both pre-shared entanglement and classical communication.

questions.question: In superdense coding, transmission of one qubit can communicate
questions.explanation: Superdense coding transmits 2 classical bits using 1 qubit and shared entanglement.

questions.question: Which theorem states that an unknown quantum state cannot be copied exactly?
questions.explanation: The no-cloning theorem prevents exact copying of unknown quantum states.

questions.question: The main advantage of Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) is
questions.explanation: QKD detects eavesdropping because observation disturbs quantum states.

title: Week 10: Bloch Sphere & Multiplexing
description: Bloch sphere geometric state representation, microwave pulse manipulation, Single Electron Transistors (SET), quantum dots, FDMA, TDMA, and SDMA.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of the Bloch sphere?
questions.explanation: The Bloch sphere provides a graphical representation of all possible states of a single qubit.

questions.question: Which signal is commonly used to manipulate a superconducting qubit?
questions.explanation: Microwave pulses are used to rotate and manipulate qubit states with high precision.

questions.question: Why is single-qubit control important in quantum computing?
questions.explanation: Single-qubit control is essential for implementing quantum gates and building larger quantum algorithms.

questions.question: If a qubit is in the state |ψ⟩ = 0.6|0⟩ + 0.8|1⟩, what is the probability of measuring |1⟩?
questions.explanation: Measurement probability equals the square of the amplitude: P(1) = |0.8|^2 = 0.64 = 64%.

questions.question: In a silicon two-qubit device, charge sensing is commonly performed using a
questions.explanation: SETs are extremely sensitive charge detectors widely used for qubit readout.

questions.question: In silicon quantum processors, qubits are often formed using
questions.explanation: Silicon qubits are commonly realized using quantum dots created under gate electrodes.

questions.question: FDMA multiplexing separates qubits using
questions.explanation: FDMA assigns a unique operating frequency to each qubit channel.

questions.question: Which multiplexing technique provides sequential access to qubits?
questions.explanation: TDMA allocates different time slots to different qubits, resulting in sequential access.

questions.question: What is the primary advantage of SDMA?
questions.explanation: SDMA uses separate spatial paths, allowing simultaneous operation with reduced interference.

questions.question: A quantum circuit consists primarily of
questions.explanation: A quantum circuit is built from qubits, quantum gates, and measurement operations.

title: Week 11: Quantum Metrology & Readout
description: Quantum sensors, Single Photon Avalanche Diodes (SPAD), Geiger mode, decoherence, spin-to-charge conversion, QPC/SET amplifiers, and ADC digitization.

questions.question: What is the primary objective of quantum metrology?
questions.explanation: Quantum metrology uses quantum effects to achieve measurement precision beyond classical limits.

questions.question: Quantum sensing derives its advantage mainly from
questions.explanation: Quantum sensing relies on maintaining coherence and exploiting entanglement.

questions.question: Which parameter most directly limits readout fidelity?
questions.explanation: Poor detector efficiency causes loss of information during measurement and directly reduces readout fidelity.

questions.question: SPAD stands for
questions.explanation: SPAD stands for Single-Photon Avalanche Diode.

questions.question: A SPAD detects single photons while operating in
questions.explanation: A SPAD operates above breakdown voltage in Geiger mode.

questions.question: The loss of quantum information due to interaction with the environment is called
questions.explanation: Environmental interactions disturb quantum states and destroy coherence, known as decoherence.

questions.question: Why is calibration of quantum sensors challenging?
questions.explanation: Quantum sensors must ultimately be referenced to classical standards, making calibration challenging.

questions.question: In spin-qubit readout, the spin state is first converted into
questions.explanation: Spin states are converted into a detectable charge configuration for readout.

questions.question: Which block amplifies the weak output signal from a QPC/SET with minimum added noise?
questions.explanation: The Low-Noise Amplifier (LNA) boosts weak signals with minimal added noise.

questions.question: After amplification and filtering, which circuit converts the analog signal into digital form?
questions.explanation: The ADC converts the amplified analog signal into digital data.

title: Week 12: Advanced Transport & S-Parameters
description: FDSOI subthreshold saturation, transconductance enhancement, S-parameters on Smith charts, NEGF quantum transport, f_MAX, and Zero Temp Coeff (ZTC).

questions.question: As temperature decreases from 300 K to 5.5 K, the subthreshold slope (SS) of an FDSOI MOSFET generally
questions.explanation: Subthreshold slope improves (decreases) with temperature and then saturates at extremely low temperatures due to incomplete ionization or self-heating.

questions.question: The improvement in NMOS transconductance at cryogenic temperatures is primarily due to
questions.explanation: Reduced phonon scattering at low temperatures increases carrier mobility and transconductance.

questions.question: Which parameter is commonly extracted from measured S-parameters using a small signal equivalent circuit model?
questions.explanation: Intrinsic transconductance and parasitic elements are extracted from S-parameters.

questions.question: If the intrinsic transconductance of an NMOS improves by 39% from a room temperature value of 10 mS, the new value is closest to
Which graphical tool is commonly used to compare measured and modeled S parameters?
questions.explanation: The Smith chart is standard for plotting and comparing reflection and transmission S-parameters.

questions.question: If the source resistance decreases by 12% from 100 Ω, the new resistance is
The NEGF formalism is primarily used to model
questions.explanation: Nonequilibrium Green's Function (NEGF) formalism is the standard method for modeling quantum transport.

questions.question: As channel length becomes extremely small, which leakage mechanism becomes increasingly important?
questions.explanation: In nanoscale transistors, source-to-drain tunneling becomes a dominant leakage mechanism.

questions.question: The maximum oscillation frequency f_MAX is
options: The frequency where transconductance is maximum
The frequency at which Mason's unilateral power gain (U) = 1
The frequency where threshold voltage shifts
questions.explanation: f_MAX is defined as the frequency where Mason's unilateral power gain U equals 1.

questions.question: What is the Zero Temperature Coefficient (ZTC) point in ID–VGS characteristics?
options: The bias point where threshold voltage is minimum
The point where ID reaches maximum
The bias point where drain current (ID) remains nearly constant across different temperatures
The point where subthreshold slope (SS) is independent of channel length
questions.explanation: At the ZTC bias point, mobility degradation and threshold voltage shifts cancel out, making drain current nearly independent of temperature.

title: Week 13: Comprehensive Practice Assessment
description: Capstone synthesis covering work-function differences, carrier freeze-out, Fermi-Dirac statistics, CNOT logic, thermal noise kT, and Varshni bandgap widening.

questions.question: In the energy band diagram, the potential difference between the vacuum level and the Fermi level of the metal in a MOS device is known as
questions.explanation: The potential difference between the vacuum level and the Fermi level of the metal is known as the work-function difference.

questions.question: What condition leads to carrier freeze-out in semiconductors?
questions.explanation: Very low temperatures cause thermal energy to be insufficient for dopant ionization, leading to carrier freeze-out.

questions.question: The Fermi–Dirac distribution function f(E) gives the probability that
options: A state is in the conduction band
An electron occupies a quantum state at energy E
An electron is excited to the valence band
questions.explanation: The Fermi-Dirac distribution function specifies the probability that an electron occupies a quantum state at energy E.

questions.question: Which quantum gate performs the equivalent of a classical XOR operation on two qubits?
questions.explanation: The CNOT gate acts as a conditional NOT operation, performing the quantum equivalent of a classical XOR.

questions.question: The Heisenberg Uncertainty Principle states that
options: Light behaves only as a wave
It is possible to know both position and momentum precisely
questions.explanation: The position and momentum uncertainty relation is given by Δx · Δp ≥ ℏ.

questions.question: A classical bit differs from a qubit because it
options: Can store more than two values
Can exist in a probabilistic state
Is always in a definite 0 or 1 state
questions.explanation: A classical bit is strictly binary and always in a definite 0 or 1 state, unlike a qubit which can exist in superposition.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about cryogenic electronics is true?
options: They require a higher voltage supply
They help maintain qubit stability by reducing noise
They are only used in mobile computing
questions.explanation: Cryogenic electronics operate at very low temperatures to reduce thermal noise and help maintain qubit stability.

questions.question: Which physical relationship governs thermal noise?
options: kT, where T is the absolute temperature
questions.explanation: Thermal noise power is proportional to kT, where k is Boltzmann's constant and T is absolute temperature.

questions.question: According to the Varshni model, how does the bandgap energy (Eg) change with decreasing temperature?
questions.explanation: According to the Varshni model, the semiconductor bandgap widens (increases) as temperature decreases.

questions.question: What does the acronym MOSFET stand for?
options: Metal Oxide Semiconductor Field Effect Transistor
Metal Oxide Silicon Field Effect Transistor
Metal Oxide Semiconductor Fast Electron Transistor
Metal On Semiconductor Field Effect Transistor
questions.explanation: MOSFET stands for Metal Oxide Semiconductor Field Effect Transistor.
